title: Living with atrial fibrillation
what: With atrial fibrillation, the heart beats unevenly. The main danger is blood clots and stroke, so medicines and check-ups matter.
why: If a doctor found atrial fibrillation on your ECG.
duration: treatment is usually long-term; check-ups with your doctor follow a schedule
tell_doctor: If you feel skipped beats, a racing heart, or shortness of breath
All your medicines and supplements, especially blood thinners
If you have had any bleeding
Before any surgery or tooth removal

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take them every day. Do not skip them or stop them on your own.

prepare.title: Pulse
prepare.text: Learn to count your pulse, or use a blood pressure monitor that detects an irregular heartbeat.

prepare.title: Other doctors
prepare.text: Tell every doctor and dentist which medicines you take.

bring: Your latest ECG and medical papers
A diary of your blood pressure and pulse
steps: Take your medicines every day at the same time
Measure your blood pressure and pulse and write them down
Limit alcohol, since it often triggers episodes
Get enough sleep and move every day
Have the tests your doctor ordered
feel: Sometimes you feel skipped beats or fluttering in your chest
Many people feel nothing, and that is also normal
after: Watch for signs of bleeding if you take blood thinners
Do not start new medicines or herbs without asking your doctor
Tell your family the signs of a stroke
red_flags: Drooping face, a weak arm, or trouble speaking: call emergency services
Chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or fainting: call emergency services
Blood in the urine, black stools, or heavy bleeding: see a doctor urgently

faq.a: By itself it often does not threaten life, but it raises the risk of stroke. Treatment lowers that risk.
Moderate exercise is usually good for you. Choose it together with your doctor.

reminders.text: Time for your heart medicine. Check your pulse and blood pressure.
